text:
incident-bot: ALERT: runtime-canary us-west-2 (v3.4.1-canary) — p95 latency spike and elevated 5xxs. p95=980ms (SLO 300ms), 5xx=1.8% (>0.5% threshold). Autoscale okay. Triggered paging to #incidents.
amy_oncall: I'm taking this. First glance — did this follow a release?
eng_raul: yes — rollout r-20260317-42 finished ~03:12 UTC. Canary only. Seeing many kernel-fallback logs (~kv eviction + fallback to slow kernels) and microbatch queue growth.
amy_oncall: copy. Can you paste the kernel-fallback log sample?
eng_raul: here: ```[2026-03-17T03:18:07Z] worker-22 kernel_select: fallback_to_generic_kernel reason=quant-mismatch seq_len=256 latency_regressed=true```
sre_mike: also seeing continuous small batch flushes that leak latency; batch windows collapsing -> more single-token batches. Potentially a batching heuristic change in this canary.
amy_oncall: support_lead_sam — any customer-facing errors?
support_lead_sam: CS reports tickets from two customers (enterprise-us-west) complaining that request latency jumped and a few timeouts. No major outage yet, but they're seeing degraded UX.
eng_jenny: confirmed config diff: canary toggled new batching heuristic and new kernel selector codepath. Changeset r-20260317-42 -> modules: batcher:v2, kernel-selector:prefer-quantized.
amy_oncall: ok mitigation options: 1) flip feature flag for new batcher on canary 2) rollback canary release 3) force kernel selector to legacy. We should try lowest-impact quick fix first.
eng_raul: I can flip the canary batcher flag now. Flag name: `ff.new_batcher_canary` in featureflags service. Command: `redwoodctl feature toggle ff.new_batcher_canary --env canary --off`
amy_oncall: do it and watch telemetry. Also prepare rollback command if flip doesn't help: `redwoodctl rollout rollback --id r-20260317-42 --target-tag stable-20260316`
eng_raul: toggled off at 03:24:12 UTC. Watching metrics...
incident-bot: NOTE: feature-flag change detected by audit-log (actor=eng_raul, flag=ff.new_batcher_canary, env=canary, action=OFF)
sre_mike: p95 trending down to 420ms now, 5xx down to 0.6%. Improvement but still above SLO.
eng_jenny: kernel-selector still showing repeated fallback events; toggling batcher reduced churn but kernel path may need forced selector fallback. We can opt for `redwoodctl set-config kernel_selector.mode=legacy --env canary` to force legacy selection. That is low risk for canary.
amy_oncall: do it if metric doesn't hit SLO in next 6 minutes. If it doesn't help, proceed with full rollback.
platform_ops: manual kernel selector override applied at 03:31:04 UTC (operator=platform_ops).
incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: kernel_selector.mode=legacy applied (actor=platform_ops, env=canary)
sre_mike: p95 now at 280ms, 5xx at 0.25% — back under SLO. Nice.
support_lead_sam: CS: telling customers it's a canary regression and we've mitigated; no broad customer impact. Sam to monitor for follow-ups.
amy_oncall: summary for handoff: canary rollout r-20260317-42 triggered batching heuristic/kernel selector mismatch causing kernel fallback and microbatch thrash -> p95 and 5xx spike in us-west canary only. Actions taken: 1) ff.new_batcher_canary toggled OFF 2) kernel_selector.mode forced to legacy in canary 3) telemetry closely monitored. Current state: metrics restored to SLO.
amy_oncall: mitigations left: - run a narrow e2e test of kernel-selector+batcher interactions in staging before re-promoting - add guardrail to kernel selector to avoid quant-path mismatches - create postmortem runbook item to require A/B perf tests on kernel-selector changes.
amy_oncall: handing to sre_mike for 2-hour watch and artifact collection. Please escalate if we see >0.5% 5xx or p95>350ms.
sre_mike: taking it. I'll keep a watch dashboard up and capture traces.
eng_raul: will open PR to revert kernel-selector change from canary branch and add stricter selector metrics.
eng_jenny: adding a quick check in CI to catch batching window collapse patterns.
support_lead_sam: CS notified customers with a short blurb. No wider customer impact.
amy_oncall: thanks team. Closing page but not the thread. If anything resurfaces, @sre_mike please reopen.
platform_ops: logging incident state in incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-20260317-42
sre_mike: note for postmortem: timeline + config diffs + sample traces saved at /var/artifacts/INC-20260317-42/ . I'll include sampling of affected requests for root-cause analysis.
amy_oncall: handoff complete.
